name: Does hardwood hold up well in Colorado kitchens?

mainEntity.name: Does hardwood hold up well in Colorado kitchens?

acceptedAnswer.text: In our Front Range climate, rapid shifts in indoor humidity between dry winters and wetter seasons cause natural wood to expand and contract significantly. While hardwood can perform well in kitchens across Denver, Centennial, and Parker, engineered hardwood is generally a more stable choice than solid wood. It resists seasonal gapping and cupping much better under fluctuating indoor air moisture. If you prefer the warmth of wood, ensure your home maintains consistent indoor humidity, clean standing water quickly, and consider durable protective finishes designed for kitchen traffic.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hardwood works well if humidity is maintained, but engineered wood is more stable in Colorado's dry, shifting climate to prevent gapping and moisture-related warping.
